Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies on the tower above the walled town in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780). No other flag is shown, so the pictures never say who held the Rock before that or who the attackers are.
Q2: "1779 — The Great Siege" (frame 23). It shows a big camp of white tents and a long line of animals or wagons on land, and later ships at sea (frames 22-39). The pictures alone don't say who besieges whom.
Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger directly. The most they suggest is that land and sea are cut off: a siege camp, a convoy line, and ships circling offshore. There is no food, starving people or text about hunger.
Q4: Ships. A fleet of sailing ships approaches the town in Jan 1780 (frame 47), and a column of small figures with red cargo or barrels reaches the bastion (frames 48-49). The pictures don't say if these are a relief fleet, and they don't clearly show that the town is rescued.
